item.title: Hi malagatravelguide.net Webmaster!
item.content:encoded:
Zac Anthon zac.anthon@gmail.com Hi malagatravelguide.net Webmaster! Would you like this New Year to be the year you let go of your hurtful past? Make the resolution to make the change to become your Best Self.
Have you heard of Se-REM? (Self effective - Rapid Eye Movement). Many people don't know that REM brain activity dramatically improves the processing of traumatic emotion. It creates peace and empowers the listener. Se-REM is an advanced version of EMDR therapy. It is more powerful because it combines elements of 6 different therapies, EMDR, hypnosis, mindfulness, Gestalt child within work, music therapy, and Awe therapy, (connecting profoundly with nature). Classical music alternates between the ears to enhance daydreaming and visualizing in ways you have never experienced. Please read the many reviews that express how much it has helped. It has helped thousands of people overcome PTSD, and anxiety. But it is also helpful in a great many situations, any experience that has been traumatic. Se-REM's mission statement is "Trauma relief at as close to free as possible". This not-for-profit program downloads to a smart phone or computer and can be used at home. Read and download at: Se-REM.com. Once you own the program, you are encouraged to give it away to others who will benefit. item.title: question
item.content:encoded: Brent Kent kent.brent@yahoo.com question Have you heard of Se-REM? (Self effective - Rapid Eye Movement). Many people don't know that REM brain activity dramatically improves the processing of traumatic emotion. It creates peace and empowers the listener. Se-REM is an advanced version of EMDR therapy. It is more powerful because it combines elements of 6 different therapies, EMDR, hypnosis, mindfulness, Gestalt child within work, music therapy, and Awe therapy, (connecting profoundly with nature). Classical music alternates between the ears to enhance daydreaming and visualizing in ways you have never experienced. Please read the many reviews that express how much it has helped. It has helped thousands of people overcome PTSD, and anxiety. But it is also helpful in a great many situations, any experience that has been traumatic. Se-REM's mission statement is "Trauma relief at as close to free as possible". This not-for-profit program downloads to a smart phone or computer and can be used at home. Read and download at: Se-REM.com. Once you own the program, you are encouraged to give it away to others who will benefit. Wondering how to carve out your slice of this multi-million dollar pie?
The answer is creating in-demand, stunning graphics that buyers are eager to use.
And for that, there's no better shortcut than StockDreams: https://www.getprofitnow.info/stockdream

StockDreams hands you an extensive array of templates—plus ongoing additions—enabling you to craft eye-catching designs right out of the gate, skill level notwithstanding. Absolute beginners? You bet.

item.title: Thrive Leads v Optin Monster: Email list building
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
A little of topic you think? ... Not really, let me tell you why. A few months ago I was trying to think of ways to reach out to our community here on Malaga Travel Guide and realised for all the people that email me and comment on my posts I don't really have a medium to harness all this feedback. I wanted a way to communicate faster with my audience so I can give you all my best info as fast as possible and whats faster than email right? I thought the best way forward to help build this blog and community was to build an email list. Now, there are many ways to grow an email list but one of the fastest ways is to capture email addresses in return for a free guide, ebook or wordpress plugin something helpful to my audience. this can be done via In steps the two main players in the Wordpress plugin popup market.
  • Thrive Leads
  • Optin Monster

What You Will Learn

  • Whats the main differences?
  • Is Optin Monster worth the extra moolah?
  • Is there a steep learning curve to implement?
  • Tutorials and updates - getting started
  • What is the Support Level like?
  • Do this software come with any guarantees?
  • A step by step guide on how to implement Thrive Leads

 Installation

I installed Optin Monster in a breeze its a simple Wordpress plugin installation and Thrive Leads was about 10MB so I installed this via ftp as a lot of hosting account prevent large file uploads and place restrictions on your account. If you have a problem please contact your host make sure to explain this. There are also many tutorials on ftp uploading using a free software program, Filezilla is one of the most popular ones

Optinmonster Comparison

Optin Monster is onto version 2 at the moment and comes in a few different flavours to target single sites licenses, multi site licenses and agencies. This is the market leader before Thrive Leads came onto the scene. Yeah yeah I know you hate these popup suckers but guess what most people feel the same but they work. You may have seen this popup before? Yeah I thought you would recognize it. Some find these popups rather annoying and they can be but there are few ways to implement to reduce the pain.

Pricing Of Optinmonster/Thrive Leads

As you can see the basic 1 license is 49 USD compared to Thrive Leads 37 USD (This goes up on Tuesday 24th February midnight) The real difference between the two on pricing is when you get to multilicenses with the pro coming ion at nearly 200 dollars and Thrive Leads in at 67 USD (price rises to 97 USD Tuesday 24th February) Let me show you how Thrive Leads can help you target readers on 5 different angles

Lead groups

There are a number of ways to get the best out of Thrive Leads, the main opt-in form types include:
  • Ribbons
  • Popovers
  • Widgets
  • After post
  • Slide-ins

item.title: Best Things to do in Marbella
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
The Ultimate Guide to Marbella: Top Things to Do for Young Adventurers

Introduction

Welcome to Marbella, the Costa del Sol’s playground! With sun-soaked beaches, a buzzing nightlife, and a mix of cool cultural spots, Marbella is the perfect destination for young travelers looking to soak up the sun and party. Whether you're into chilling on the beach, hitting the clubs, or exploring, Marbella has got you covered. Let’s dive into the best things to do!

1. Explore the Old Town (Casco Antiguo)

Kick off your Marbella adventure in the charming Old Town. Get lost in the narrow, winding streets filled with cute shops and vibrant street art. Plaza de los Naranjos is the perfect spot to grab a coffee or a refreshing drink at one of the lively cafes. Don’t forget to snap some pics for the 'Gram in front of the stunning Iglesia de la Encarnación—it’s super Instagrammable!

2. Chill at the Beaches

Marbella’s beaches are where the real fun begins! Hit up Playa de la Fontanilla for a chill day with friends, or get your party on at Nikki Beach, where the vibes are always high, and the music is pumping. Want some adventure? Try out jet skiing or paddleboarding to spice up your beach day!

3. Party at Puerto Banús

If you’re looking for luxury and nightlife, Puerto Banús is the place to be. Check out the swanky yachts, browse the designer shops, and then transition into party mode as the sun sets. Grab dinner at a trendy restaurant, then dance the night away at one of the buzzing clubs. It’s the ultimate spot for people-watching and soaking up the glamorous atmosphere!

4. Get Active Outdoors

For those who love the outdoors, Marbella offers awesome activities beyond the beach. Hit the Sierra de las Nieves for epic hikes with jaw-dropping views, or grab your friends for a round of golf at one of the many courses. You can also cycle along the coastal paths for a more relaxed way to take in the stunning scenery.

5. Eat Like a Local

Food is a huge part of the Marbella experience! Dive into the local cuisine with some delicious tapas at one of the many trendy bars in the Old Town. Try the iconic espeto de sardinas (grilled sardines), or get creative and sample a variety of dishes with friends. For a special night out, book a table at a chic restaurant like Trocadero Arena—the vibe is unbeatable!

6. Discover the Culture

Balance your beach days with some culture! The Museo del Grabado Español Contemporáneo has cool exhibitions that’ll impress your art-loving friends. Check out the Bonsai Museum for something unique—it’s a hidden gem that’s definitely worth a visit. If you’re in town during local festivals, like San Bernabé Festival, join the celebrations for an unforgettable experience!

7. Day Trips for Adventure

Feeling adventurous? Take a day trip to Ronda, a stunning town famous for its breathtaking views and dramatic cliffs. It’s a great spot for Instagram-worthy shots! Alternatively, explore nearby natural parks for hiking or simply enjoying nature. Whether you rent a car or join a group tour, there’s plenty to explore just outside Marbella.

Conclusion

Marbella is the perfect mix of relaxation, adventure, and fun for young travelers. With its stunning beaches, vibrant nightlife, and rich culture, there’s never a dull moment. Grab your friends, pack your bags, and get ready for an unforgettable experience in this Costa del Sol paradise!

item.title: Things to do in Marbella in Winter
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
Winter in Marbella brings a different, more relaxed charm to the city than the busy summer months. Here are some great things to do during this cooler season:

1. Explore the Old Town (Casco Antiguo)

  • The heart of Marbella’s historic center is filled with narrow streets, whitewashed buildings, and colorful flower pots. Orange Square (Plaza de los Naranjos) is particularly charming during winter with its cozy cafes and traditional Spanish architecture.
  • This is a perfect spot to try local churros with chocolate or a warm café con leche.

2. Enjoy Marbella’s Beaches

  • While it may not be beach weather, Marbella's beaches are still beautiful for walking. La Fontanilla, Playa de la Venus, and Puerto Banús beaches are scenic with far fewer crowds.
  • The boardwalk along the beaches is ideal for a leisurely stroll or bike ride, with great sunset views over the Mediterranean.

3. Hiking in the Sierra Blanca Mountains

  • For outdoor enthusiasts, the Sierra Blanca mountains offer incredible winter hiking opportunities. The cooler temperatures make it an ideal season for hiking.
  • La Concha is a popular peak that offers breathtaking views of Marbella and the coastline. La Concha translated into English is 'The Shell', the mountain is named due to it's stark resemblance to a sea shell.

4. Visit Puerto Banús Marina

  • Winter brings a quieter, more peaceful vibe to this famous luxury marina. You can stroll along the port to admire yachts, luxury cars, and designer boutiques without the usual summer crowds.
  • Nearby restaurants and cafes still offer great food and drinks, many with outdoor heaters for a cozy winter experience.

5. Indulge in Spanish Tapas and Wine

  • Many tapas bars and restaurants offer traditional Spanish dishes, perfect for warming up on chilly days. Head to areas like Alameda Park or Old Town for authentic Spanish dining.
  • Winter is a great time to try heartier Andalusian dishes like puchero (a traditional stew), cocido madrileño, and locally sourced wine.

6. Play Golf at Marbella’s Renowned Courses

  • Marbella is famous for its golf courses, and many people find winter to be the best season for playing golf. Some popular courses include La Quinta, Los Naranjos, and Marbella Golf & Country Club.
  • The cooler weather allows you to comfortably enjoy the game while still soaking up Marbella’s sunshine.

7. Explore Nearby Towns and Villages

  • Winter is an ideal time to take day trips to charming nearby towns like Ronda, Mijas Pueblo, and Estepona. Each town offers a different glimpse of Andalusian culture and history.
  • Ronda’s dramatic cliffs and ancient bridges are especially stunning in winter, and Mijas Pueblo has a picturesque mountain setting that’s cozy and charming.

8. Relax at a Spa or Wellness Center

  • Marbella has several high-end spas, wellness centers, and hammams that offer luxury treatments and relaxation, perfect for unwinding in the winter months.
  • Many of the larger hotels, like the Marbella Club Hotel, offer day passes for their wellness facilities if you’re not a guest.

9. Visit Local Art Galleries and Museums

  • The Ralli Museum is a hidden gem featuring Latin American and European contemporary art. It’s free to enter and offers a unique artistic experience.
  • The Museo del Grabado Español Contemporáneo is another local museum focusing on Spanish contemporary engraving and prints, showcasing works by Picasso, Dalí, and Miró.

10. Attend Local Winter Festivals and Events

  • Winter in Marbella has several festive events. Christmas lights, decorations, and seasonal markets pop up around December, especially along Avenida del Mar and Orange Square.
  • The Three Kings Parade (Cabalgata de los Reyes) on January 5th is a Spanish tradition worth seeing if you’re in Marbella early in the year.

11. Explore Alameda Park and Avenida del Mar

  • Alameda Park, with its subtropical plants and fountains, is a peaceful green space to enjoy during winter. It’s close to the beach and Old Town.
  • Avenida del Mar is an open-air pedestrian street with impressive Salvador Dalí sculptures, offering an outdoor gallery experience.

12. Take a Day Trip to Sierra Nevada for Skiing

  • Just a couple of hours away, the Sierra Nevada ski resort offers skiing and snowboarding. It’s a fun way to combine Marbella’s mild winter climate with the thrill of snow sports on the same trip.

Marbella's winter offers a mild Mediterranean climate with plenty of sunshine, so it's a great time to explore the city and its surroundings without the high-season crowds.

item.title: My Scoop as an Expat Living in Spain
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
Travel Blogger / Exercise Junkie / Mummy

Hi, I'm Suzy, an English expat lucky enough to be living in beautiful Malaga on the Costa del Sol.  My passion and reason for this blog is to bring my readers the best travel advice on what to do in this diverse region of Spain. Having spent the last 15 years of my life with my husband and now 12 year old daughter living in Spain, my aim is to share my knowledge of the places I know and those I am still discovering with you, my loyal readers. Malaga city holds a special place in my heart, I've witnessed how this city has developed in the 15 years I have lived here to what it is now.  It's ever changing and in my opinion just keeps getting better and better. Malaga province is vast and much of it I am still to explore, as I do I will bring you updates on real life experiences of this wonderfully diverse region. For now I will tell you all I know about the places I've been to, from restaurants and bars to children's play parks and beaches. Each post is written from personal experience and researched by me, if there's something I've missed or you wish to add, I invite you to leave a comment. I always respond and engage with my readers as it is you that help make this blog what it is. I don't get paid for what I write,  all I ask is that you please share my posts with your friends and like my page on Facebook. I would be very grateful for any love and support you can give my blog. Suzy :-)

item.title: Thinking About Breast Implants? Don’t Until You’ve Read my Story
item.dc:creator: administrator

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value:
“How come you ended up with big boobs?”

That’s what my mum and sister used to say to me, going back to when I was in my teens and into my twenties.

I was quite slim but with a nice full C cup…. why do we never appreciate what we’ve got until it’s quite literally gone?

When I hit my early thirties I noticed some of the fullness was disappearing, probably years of running and high impact exercise not wearing a decent sports bra.  But also age and gravity too.

At 35 I was pregnant and despite what I'd hoped, my boobs didn’t really get that much bigger during pregnancy. Maybe they were just a little bit fuller but I liked them, they reminded me of when I was younger.

Of course once I had my daughter and stopped breast feeding, the inevitable happened and so for the last 4 years I have been left with empty sagging skin where my nice full boobs once where.

Clothes shop nightmares

Shopping for clothes post child birth was rarely an enjoyable experience.  Everything I tried on revolved around, whether I would look half decent in one of my numerous under-wired, push up, extra padded bras.

Bikini shopping was even more soul destroying, some of my bikini tops had that much padding it was unbelievable that there was any room left for my boobs.

You get the picture, like many mums I have been unhappy with my boobs since having my daughter.

So for the last 4 years and especially every year when it comes round to summer and wearing less clothing, I would feel very self conscious about my upper body.

My family and friends would comment that I looked too skinny and I should put weight on. I work hard in the gym to stay slim and I definitely don’t want to look skinny but no amount of chest presses or push ups would ever change the appearance of my boobs.

If I do put weight on, because I’m more pear shaped it just goes to my hips and bum, not my chest, leaving me looking really out of proportion.

The camera never lies​

I think the turning point for me was when we were on holiday towards the end of summer 2015 and my husband took some photos of me drinking a Mojito on the beach.

I was wearing a black bandeau type bikini top, which had the usual padding.

At the time I thought I looked alright in it if I’m honest, but when I looked back at the photos I was gutted at how scrawny I looked….the camera never lies so they say.

I couldn’t stop looking at this picture and hating what I saw but I never thought I would ever consider getting boob implants in my life. I just never thought it was for me.

Living on the Costa del Sol you just need to take a ﻿walk around Marbella and Puerto Banus to see that loads of women have had breast augmentation.  Cosmetic surgery is huge on the Costa del Sol but there are a lot of ‘fake’ looking boob jobs around and that’s really not my thing.

Mid life crisis?​

Christmas came and went, I turned 40 and it was on my mind again.

Maybe I was having a bit of a mid life crisis but as spring was around the corner I started to get a little paranoid about having to wear a bikini and summer clothes again.

I spoke to a couple of close friends who already had implants and more or less everyone said the same thing.

“It’s the best thing I’ve ever done” or “It’s the best money I’ve ever spent”.

I decided to take the plunge and book consultations with a couple of plastic surgeons to see what they would suggest, easily done being in Marbella where there are plenty of top plastic surgeons.

Before and after breast implants photos

I did some research and started becoming a bit obsessed with googling pictures of before and after breast implants.  

I kind of knew that by taking this step, I had half made my mind up. Although I told myself I was just getting quotes and doing a bit of research, I mean how much are boob jobs these days anyway? I was curious to know.

It was when I arranged my second appointment with one particular surgeon that I knew this was it, I was going to commit to having it done. I liked him from the start, he was friendly, personable and seemed to completely understand what I wanted and I think because he almost seemed to approve of the look I was after.

I made it clear in both consultations that I did not want big boobs, they were empty and I wanted the volume and fullness back, I didn’t want the implant to be visible and just wanted a very natural look. I said I was conscious of my ribs and chest bones being on show and that it made me look skinny.

He said he understood completely and pointed out that I had very thin skin on my chest and around my boobs and this was why my ribs showed through my skin. This made perfect sense to me; I wasn’t too skinny, just my skin was skinny!

Size matters!​

I liked that he got what my objectives were and straight away he suggested 375cc (cc's = cubic centimetres) moderate profile round Silicone implants placed under the muscle (as this would give a more natural look). He would do an inframammary incision, which is where the lower part of the breast meets the chest wall, basically the breast fold.

I don’t really care about slight scarring on the fold as ill never go topless anyway. I freaked out a bit about the size and told him that that 375cc sounded big on my frame, but what do I know….

He reassured me that they wouldn’t be big, the moderate profile implant gives a more natural look with less fullness in the upper part of the breast than the high profile implant so they wouldn’t stick out as much and be so noticeable.

He gave me a price which I was kind of surprised with but in a good way since it was a massive €3000 cheaper than one quote I'd had.  He answered all my questions about recovery and when I can exercise etc.

So I confirmed with the surgeons secretary a few days later and we agreed the date and time I was going to have the op which was about 3 weeks away. That was it; I was booked in to have actual breast implants!!

Am I doing the right thing?​

I couldn’t quite believe it and from that day I can honestly say right up until the day of surgery I probably changed my mind at least 10 times. I had loads of personal reasons to be unsure if I was doing the right thing:

  • I hated the thought of not being able to do proper exercise for at least 6 weeks
  • I was worried about what people would think of me
  • I was worried they would look unnatural and I would want to cover them up
  • I was worried I wouldn't be able to do anything around the house or take care of my daughter properly
  • I was worried about the actual surgery and whether there would be any complications during or whilst I was recovering
  • I felt selfish spending so much money on a cosmetic procedure that could have gotten us a great family holiday or 100 other things

Despite all of these concerns I didn’t cancel but I decided I would only tell the people closest to me and those who I felt would be supportive of my decision.  I didn't even tell my mum and sister because I was worried about their opinion on cosmetic surgery and thought they would really disapprove.  

I obviously didn't give them enough credit as once I did tell them (3 weeks after surgery) they were actually really happy for me.  My mum even said she would have come over to help out if I had told her what I was doing, I think she was probably wishing I had so she could have come to Spain for a little holiday too.

3  MAIN AREAS OF RESEARCH TO FOCUS ON

After deciding that I wanted to go ahead with the surgery I concentrated my research on 3 areas:

RESEARCH

Finding a board certified surgeon with lots of experience in your cosmetic procedure is crucial to achieving the best result.

COST SAVINGS

Compare costs and take into account travel expenses if opting for surgery abroad. Beware - The cheapest may not always be the best.

AFTER CARE

Good after care should be high on your priority list. Listen to your surgeon's instructions post op and keep all follow up appointments. 

Know your surgeon

Important to mention that before committing to surgery one thing I made a point of doing was checking out my surgeon’s credentials. Depending on where you decide to have your surgery each country or region will have a directory of board certified surgeons.

You should always check your surgeon is fully licensed and registered even if you are going on a recommendation.

Get as much information as possible, check out their profile on the hospitals website he or she operates at, it should list their expertise, experience and qualifications.

Don’t be afraid to ask them what qualifications and experience he or she has for carrying out this operation and ask them for genuine testimonials from previous patients.

My ﻿plastic ﻿surgeon is registered with the following:

  • SECPRE – Spanish Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.
  • SACPRE – Andalucían Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.
  • ASPS – American Society of Plastic surgeons.

​Recommendations are always good but bear in mind that one surgeon who is right for your friend may not be right for you. This is a big decision you're making and you need to be sure that everything looks and feels exactly right.

If you enjoyed my story and are interested in seeing the results, then follow on to read about the day of my breast implant surgery as well as top recovery tips.​

I liked that he got what my objectives were and straight away he suggested 375cc (cc's = cubic centimetres) moderate profile round Silicone implants placed under the muscle (as this would give a more natural look). He would do an inframammary incision, which is where the lower part of the breast meets the chest wall, basically the breast fold.

I don’t really care about slight scarring on the fold as ill never go topless anyway. I freaked out a bit about the size and told him that that 375cc sounded big on my frame, but what do I know….

He reassured me that they wouldn’t be big, the moderate profile implant gives a more natural look with less fullness in the upper part of the breast than the high profile implant so they wouldn’t stick out as much and be so noticeable.

He gave me a price which I was kind of surprised with but in a good way since it was a massive €3000 cheaper than one quote I'd had.  He answered all my questions about recovery and when I can exercise etc.

So I confirmed with the surgeons secretary a few days later and we agreed the date and time I was going to have the op which was about 3 weeks away. That was it; I was booked in to have actual breast implants!!

Am I doing the right thing?​

I couldn’t quite believe it and from that day I can honestly say right up until the day of surgery I probably changed my mind at least 10 times. I had loads of personal reasons to be unsure if I was doing the right thing:

  • I hated the thought of not being able to do proper exercise for at least 6 weeks
  • I was worried about what people would think of me
  • I was worried they would look unnatural and I would want to cover them up
  • I was worried I wouldn't be able to do anything around the house or take care of my daughter properly
  • I was worried about the actual surgery and whether there would be any complications during or whilst I was recovering
  • I felt selfish spending so much money on a cosmetic procedure that could have gotten us a great family holiday or 100 other things

Despite all of these concerns I didn’t cancel but I decided I would only tell the people closest to me and those who I felt would be supportive of my decision.  I didn't even tell my mum and sister because I was worried about their opinion on cosmetic surgery and thought they would really disapprove.  

I obviously didn't give them enough credit as once I did tell them (3 weeks after surgery) they were actually really happy for me.  My mum even said she would have come over to help out if I had told her what I was doing, I think she was probably wishing I had so she could have come to Spain for a little holiday too.

3  MAIN AREAS OF RESEARCH TO FOCUS ON

After deciding that I wanted to go ahead with the surgery I concentrated my research on 3 areas:

RESEARCH

Finding a board certified surgeon with lots of experience in your cosmetic procedure is crucial to achieving the best result.

COST SAVINGS

Compare costs and take into account travel expenses if opting for surgery abroad. Beware - The cheapest may not always be the best.

AFTER CARE

Good after care should be high on your priority list. Listen to your surgeon's instructions post op and keep all follow up appointments. 

Know your surgeon

Important to mention that before committing to surgery one thing I made a point of doing was checking out my surgeon’s credentials. Depending on where you decide to have your surgery each country or region will have a directory of board certified surgeons.

You should always check your surgeon is fully licensed and registered even if you are going on a recommendation.

Get as much information as possible, check out their profile on the hospitals website he or she operates at, it should list their expertise, experience and qualifications.

Don’t be afraid to ask them what qualifications and experience he or she has for carrying out this operation and ask them for genuine testimonials from previous patients.

My ﻿plastic ﻿surgeon is registered with the following:

  • SECPRE – Spanish Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.
  • SACPRE – Andalucían Society of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.
  • ASPS – American Society of Plastic surgeons.

​Recommendations are always good but bear in mind that one surgeon who is right for your friend may not be right for you. This is a big decision you're making and you need to be sure that everything looks and feels exactly right.

If you enjoyed my story and are interested in seeing the results, then follow on to read about the day of my breast implant surgery as well as top recovery tips.​

“How come you ended up with big boobs?”

That’s what my mum and sister used to say to me, going back to when I was in my teens and into my twenties.

I was quite slim but with a nice full C cup…. why do we never appreciate what we’ve got until it’s quite literally gone?

When I hit my early thirties I noticed some of the fullness was disappearing, probably years of running and high impact exercise not wearing a decent sports bra.  But also age and gravity too.

At 35 I was pregnant and despite what I'd hoped, my boobs didn’t really get that much bigger during pregnancy. Maybe they were just a little bit fuller but I liked them, they reminded me of when I was younger.

Of course once I had my daughter and stopped breast feeding, the inevitable happened and so for the last 4 years I have been left with empty sagging skin where my nice full boobs once where.

Clothes shop nightmares

Shopping for clothes post child birth was rarely an enjoyable experience.  Everything I tried on revolved around, whether I would look half decent in one of my numerous under-wired, push up, extra padded bras.

Bikini shopping was even more soul destroying, some of my bikini tops had that much padding it was unbelievable that there was any room left for my boobs.

You get the picture, like many mums I have been unhappy with my boobs since having my daughter.

So for the last 4 years and especially every year when it comes round to summer and wearing less clothing, I would feel very self conscious about my upper body.

My family and friends would comment that I looked too skinny and I should put weight on. I work hard in the gym to stay slim and I definitely don’t want to look skinny but no amount of chest presses or push ups would ever change the appearance of my boobs.

If I do put weight on, because I’m more pear shaped it just goes to my hips and bum, not my chest, leaving me looking really out of proportion.

The camera never lies​

I think the turning point for me was when we were on holiday towards the end of summer 2015 and my husband took some photos of me drinking a Mojito on the beach.

I was wearing a black bandeau type bikini top, which had the usual padding.

At the time I thought I looked alright in it if I’m honest, but when I looked back at the photos I was gutted at how scrawny I looked….the camera never lies so they say.

I couldn’t stop looking at this picture and hating what I saw but I never thought I would ever consider getting boob implants in my life. I just never thought it was for me.

Living on the Costa del Sol you just need to take a ﻿walk around Marbella and Puerto Banus to see that loads of women have had breast augmentation.  Cosmetic surgery is huge on the Costa del Sol but there are a lot of ‘fake’ looking boob jobs around and that’s really not my thing.

Mid life crisis?​

Christmas came and went, I turned 40 and it was on my mind again.

Maybe I was having a bit of a mid life crisis but as spring was around the corner I started to get a little paranoid about having to wear a bikini and summer clothes again.

I spoke to a couple of close friends who already had implants and more or less everyone said the same thing.

“It’s the best thing I’ve ever done” or “It’s the best money I’ve ever spent”.

I decided to take the plunge and book consultations with a couple of plastic surgeons to see what they would suggest, easily done being in Marbella where there are plenty of top plastic surgeons.

Before and after breast implants photos

I did some research and started becoming a bit obsessed with googling pictures of before and after breast implants.  

I kind of knew that by taking this step, I had half made my mind up. Although I told myself I was just getting quotes and doing a bit of research, I mean how much are boob jobs these days anyway? I was curious to know.

It was when I arranged my second appointment with one particular surgeon that I knew this was it, I was going to commit to having it done. I liked him from the start, he was friendly, personable and seemed to completely understand what I wanted and I think because he almost seemed to approve of the look I was after.

  • I was worried about the actual surgery and whether there would be any complications during or whilst I was recovering

Let's plan your perfect holiday in the Costa del Sol

Hi I'm Suzy! Let me help you discover the beautiful Costa del Sol. I've compiled a FREE resource guide to list my top family resorts, things to do and places to visit. 

VIP Resource List

Let's Plan Your Perfect Costa Holiday

Wanna sip cocktails on a rooftop bar, soak up the rays on a golden beach or make your own chocolate bars in a quaint Spanish village? With over 11 years living in the Costa del Sol I've got you covered. Let's get started...

New? Start Here!

For a quick start download the free VIP resource list. I've compiled must see, do and stay in an easy to read A4 sheet you can print off. I've done the hard work so you don't have to.

Guides

Whats the best resort for you? Easy to read blog posts that will help you make the right decision on where to stay on the Costa del Sol. 

WHERE TO STAY

No one likes getting ripped off, and even if your not Donald Trump you can still snag a top apartment or hotel.  Its all about location baby!

VIP Resource List

Let's Plan Your Perfect Costa Holiday

Guides

WHERE TO STAY

No one likes getting ripped off, and even if your not Donald Trump you can still snag a top apartment or hotel.  Its all about location baby!

Let's plan your perfect holiday in the Costa del Sol

Hi I'm Suzy! Let me help you discover the beautiful Costa del Sol. I've compiled a quick resource list of the top family resorts, things to do and places to stay. 

Let's Plan Your Costa Holiday

Sip cocktails on a rooftop bar, soak up the rays on a golden beach or make your own chocolate bars in a quaint Spanish village? With over 11 years living in the Costa del Sol I've got you covered...

Discover the best Resorts on the Costa del Sol

Stay up to date with the latest reviews & top holiday tips and get more out of your holiday

Some Popular Posts

1

7 of The Most Authentic Flamenco shows in Andalucia

The word ‘Flamenco’ conjures up images of swarthy skinned dancers in colourful gypsy style dresses with silk shawls performing a type of mysterious dance.  Accompanied by male guitarists and singers in dark suits.

1

CAMINITO DEL WAY - 'walkway of death'

About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high known as ‘The Walkway of Death'.

1

INSIDERS TIPS TO EXPLORE AND ENJOY MALAGA CITY

Malaga city is a fantastic blend of both modern and traditional, from the 11th century Alcazaba Fortress standing proud above the city; to the impressive new marina complete with its trendy bars, restaurants and shops.

Fab Places to Stay

What's your tipple ... 5 Star Luxury on a super yacht or glamping in your private yurt?

1

LUXURY Bespoke VIP HOLIDAYS

If you want to smash the Costa with a VIP custom holiday designed around your high end requirements. Then hire me to make your dreams come true... Ferraris, yachts, VIP club passes no holds barred access to the coasts riches!

2

smallest chocolate factory in the world!

Monkey mayhem! Ever fancied making your own chocolate bars with custom fillings? Well let me organise a trip to the smallest chocolate factory in the world you wont be disappointed!

3

custom guides & travel tips

Coming soon in depth guides on the top resorts. Discover my favourite things to do that the average tourist misses out on.

7 of The Most Authentic Flamenco shows in Andalucia

The word ‘Flamenco’ conjures up images of swarthy skinned dancers in colourful gypsy style dresses with silk shawls performing a type of mysterious dance.  Accompanied by male guitarists and singers in dark suits.

1

CAMINITO DEL WAY - 'walkway of death'

About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high known as ‘The Walkway of Death'.

1

INSIDERS TIPS TO EXPLORE AND ENJOY MALAGA CITY

Malaga city is a fantastic blend of both modern and traditional, from the 11th century Alcazaba Fortress standing proud above the city; to the impressive new marina complete with its trendy bars, restaurants and shops.

Some Popular Posts

1

7 of The Most Authentic Flamenco shows in Andalucia

The word ‘Flamenco’ conjures up images of swarthy skinned dancers in colourful gypsy style dresses with silk shawls performing a type of mysterious dance.  Accompanied by male guitarists and singers in dark suits.

1

CAMINITO DEL WAY - 'walkway of death'

About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high known as ‘The Walkway of Death'.

1

INSIDERS TIPS TO EXPLORE AND ENJOY MALAGA CITY

Malaga city is a fantastic blend of both modern and traditional, from the 11th century Alcazaba Fortress standing proud above the city; to the impressive new marina complete with its trendy bars, restaurants and shops.

Fab Places to Stay

What's your tipple ... 5 Star Luxury on a super yacht or glamping in your private yurt?

item.title: Caminito del Rey - Discover a hidden jewel in the Costa del Sol
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
Everything you need to know about the Caminito del Rey is listed below including all the best resources to make your trip a memorable one

Caminito del Rey tickets

Tickets for the King's walk can be booked up to 3 months in advance usually. Tickets cost from €10 and for not much more you can include a guided tour, this is the best way to experience the walk.

Caminito del Rey parking

  1. North Entrance (Ardales): There is a designated parking area at the North Entrance of Caminito del Rey. The parking area is reasonably large and usually sufficient for visitors. However, during peak tourist season (spring and summer), it can fill up quickly. Arriving early in the day is recommended to secure a parking spot.
  2. South Entrance (El Chorro): The South Entrance has a smaller parking area compared to the North Entrance. Parking space here can also be limited, especially during busy times. Keep in mind the South is where you end the walk, not start it.
  3. Shuttle Services: Depending on the time of year and demand, there may be shuttle services available from nearby towns to the Caminito del Rey entrances. These can be a convenient option to avoid parking hassles.

Please note that parking availability and regulations can change, and it's essential to check for the most up-to-date information before your visit. It's also a good idea to make a reservation for your Caminito del Rey hike in advance, as the number of daily visitors is often limited to ensure safety.

I recommend checking the official Caminito del Rey website or contacting the relevant authorities or tourist information centers for the latest parking information and any updates that may have occurred since my last update in September 2023.

Caminito del Rey North Entrance

The North entrance is the starting point for the walk, the path is linear so the trail begins at the North and ends at the South point. Once you exit the walk at the South There is a bus which runs daily, every 30 minutes up until 7pm from between the North and South points. The cost is €2.50 per person and the driver will only accept cash.

Caminito del Rey deaths

There are no reported deaths since the restoration and re-opening of the walk, however there were several deaths during the period it was in dis-repair and closed.

Caminito del Rey contact details

You will find a contact form on the official website which you can complete in English.

Caminito del Rey map

Caminito del Rey review - [2023 - recently updated to include celebrity chefs Gordon Ramsay, Gino D'acampo and Fred Sirieux experiences visiting the "Kings Walk" in Malaga Province

Malaga to Caminito del Rey

To get from Malaga to Caminito del Rey, you have several transportation options. Here are the steps you can follow to reach Caminito del Rey from Malaga:

  1. By Car:
    • Renting a car is the most convenient option as it gives you flexibility and allows you to explore the area at your own pace.
    • Take the A-357 highway northwest from Malaga towards Ardales.
    • Follow the signs to El Chorro and Caminito del Rey. The drive should take approximately 1 hour.
    • There are parking areas near the entrance to Caminito del Rey.
  2. By Train:
    • You can take a train from Malaga to El Chorro, which is the closest train station to Caminito del Rey.
    • Trains are operated by Cercanías Malaga and the journey takes about 40-50 minutes.
    • Once you arrive at El Chorro station, you can take the bus to the North entrance to start the Camino del Rey walk. The bust stop is just next to El Chorro train station, it costs around €2 and you can pay the driver in cash.
  3. By Bus:
    • You can also take a bus from Malaga to El Chorro.
    • The bus service is operated by several companies, including Avanza and Autocares Paco Pepe.
    • The journey by bus takes about 1 to 1.5 hours.
    • Once you arrive at El Chorro, you can walk to the entrance of Caminito del Rey as mentioned above.
  4. Guided Tours:
    • Another option is to join a guided tour from Malaga to Caminito del Rey. Many tour companies offer day trips that include transportation, tickets, and a guide.

Caminito del Rey in English

Caminito del Rey Hotels:

While there are not many hotels directly adjacent to the trail itself, there are several hotels and accommodations in the surrounding areas where you can stay while visiting Caminito del Rey. The most common places to stay are in the towns of Ardales, El Chorro, and Alora. These towns are close to the trail and offer a range of lodging options. Here are some hotels near Caminito del Rey:

  1. Hotel Convento La Magdalena (Antequera): This upscale hotel is located in the nearby town of Antequera, offering a luxurious stay with beautiful views of the surrounding countryside.
  2. Hotel La Posada del Conde (Ardales): A charming boutique hotel located in the town of Ardales, which is very close to Caminito del Rey.
  3. Hotel Finca Rocabella (El Chorro): This hotel is situated in El Chorro, close to the entrance of Caminito del Rey. It's a great option for those looking for easy access to the trail.
  4. Complejo Turístico Rural La Garganta (El Chorro): Another option in El Chorro, this complex offers a range of accommodations, including apartments and cottages.
  5. Hostal Restaurante El Cruce (Alora): Located in Alora, this budget-friendly option is a short drive from Caminito del Rey.
  6. Camping El Chorro: If you prefer a more rustic experience, you can also camp in the area. Camping El Chorro is a popular choice among hikers.

Please note that it's a good idea to book your accommodation well in advance, especially during peak tourist seasons, as Caminito del Rey is a popular attraction, and accommodations can fill up quickly. Additionally, make sure to check the trail's official website or contact the local authorities for the latest information on access and availability, as conditions may change.

official website of Caminito del Rey

https://www.caminitodelrey.info/

item.title: Marbella hostels for solo travelers
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
back to Marbella Travel Guide hub page

Marbella, a sunny destination on Spain’s Costa del Sol, is popular with solo travelers looking for both relaxation and social experiences. Here are some hostels in Marbella that are ideal for solo travelers:

1. Hostel Bohemia Marbella

  • Vibe: A small, relaxed hostel in the heart of Marbella’s old town.
  • Features: Rooftop terrace, shared kitchen, and proximity to restaurants and cafes.
  • Why it’s good for solo travelers: The cozy common areas make it easy to meet fellow travelers, and the central location allows you to explore the city easily.

2. InHouse Marbella Hostel

  • Vibe: Friendly, family-run hostel located in the old town.
  • Features: Free Wi-Fi, relaxed environment, and close to Marbella’s beaches and nightlife.
  • Why it’s good for solo travelers: Offers a calm and intimate atmosphere for those who want to rest but also engage with other guests.

3. Albergue Inturjoven Marbella

  • Vibe: Budget-friendly, spacious, and located in a quieter part of town.
  • Features: Pool, large common areas, and affordable rates.
  • Why it’s good for solo travelers: Offers organized activities and a chance to meet other solo travelers, especially for those on a budget.

4. Hostel Berlin

  • Vibe:Clean, simple, and welcoming. It's quieter than a typical hostel but still offers opportunities to meet fellow travelers.
  • Features: Private rooms with en suite bathrooms rather than dorm style lodgings.
  • Why it’s good for solo travelers: Budget friendly but in a central spot, the on site cafe is a great way to meet other solo travellers. Also close to lots of other cafes and bars around the old town and a short walk to the beach.

5. The Monkey Room Marbella

  • Vibe: Simple, minimalist decor with a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Centrally located in Marbella's charming old town.
  • Features: Offers private rooms rather than dormitories, making it ideal for those who want a bit more privacy while still staying in a budget-friendly space.
  • Why it’s good for solo travelers: While it doesn’t have the party vibe of some hostels, it’s a calm, welcoming space where you can easily meet other guests in shared areas like the kitchen or the nearby cafes and bars.

These hostels all provide a mix of social spaces, central locations, and amenities suited to solo travelers looking for both interaction and relaxation.

item.title: 7 Tried and Tested Tips for Getting the Cheapest Flight to Malaga
item.dc:creator: lionelk
item.content:encoded:
Gone are the days when you pick up a return flight for 30 Euros from UK airports to Malaga. With the increase in fuel and material costs plus general airline greed you would be lucky to get to the Costa and back for less than 100 Euros these days. Coupled with the fact that it can take hours of searching the numerous different airlines for that elusive cheap price only to end up going back to your first option to book; by which time it has doubled in price, arrrgh!!! Fear not, there are still some good deals out there you just have to know where and how to look. Having been a frequent flyer from the UK to Malaga for almost a decade myself, I bring you my tried and tested tricks and tips for ensuring you find the best possible price.

Flight Comparison Site

Narrow your initial search by using a comparison site eg www.skyscanner.net. Be careful when selecting your comparison site as other "comparison" sites like Kayak and others only show a select number of airlines. Some are even setup by the airlines to limit your choices deliberately and inflate prices. Skyscanner will give you a broad selection of all of the airlines which fly to your selected airport either one-way or return depending on your selection. Either choose specific dates or select ’whole month’ or even ‘whole year’ if you are very flexible about when you can travel. The latter 2 options produce a table showing the best prices on each day throughout that month or year.   Once you have found the flight you want to book, be sure to then visit that airlines own website, enter the same dates for travel to double check the price, you may find its slightly cheaper booking direct. In most cases travelling with a different airline on your return journey will work out cheaper especially if you are flexible on what time you travel; early morning or late at night flights are always the cheaper option. Cheaper flights are available midweek as most people want to fly on a weekend.

Clear your cookies

Cookies are small text files stored on your computer used to hold data about you and your internet search history.  All reputable sites by law offer you the choice of accepting their cookie before proceeding to access data on their site. By accepting cookies you permit the website to track and use your data accordingly. This data exchange is only permitted if you accept the cookie disclaimer. Your data then passes via a small text file to the to transfer information about your search and other statistical information from your computer to the host of the website that you are browsing. Important information like your dates, flights and destination will all be recorded by the site in question i.e. they know exactly what you are searching for. Have you ever wondered why after searching for flights on your computer, for days afterwards you get related ads appearing on every web page you go on even if it is unrelated to flights? This happens because the cookies are storing information on what you have been browsing.  Then clever remarketing campaigns target you as they know exactly what pages, sites and products or services you have shown an interest in. But why clear them? Well each time you return to enter the search criteria on that same airline’s website, the information stored in the cookie the first time you visited checks to see if you are after the same flight. Hence telling the airline you are shopping around for the best deal but obviously could not get a better price so you have come back to their site for the best price. Based on this info they then have the option to raise the flight price and present a false case of scarcity. This translates into you thinking that the prices are going up and seats are disappearing fast encouraging you to buy asap. Clearing cookies is easy but the methods may differ depending on which browser you are using:

Google Chrome

Hold down the following keys at the same time: ‘Ctrl’ ‘Shift’ & ‘Delete’, the following window will open...tick the box ‘cookies and other site & data’ and select from the drop down menu the duration you have been searching for flights either ‘1 day, ‘1 week’ etc then click ‘clear browsing data’.    

Google Firefox

Follow the same instructions as for Google Chrome and the following page will appear, Select; time range to clear’ tick ‘cookies’ box and click ‘clear now’.     Internet Explorer - I would strongly encourage you to not use this operating system bundled browser as it has security issues. Depending on version of browser you goto the "cog wheel in top right corner (Tools), select (Internet Options), and on the General Tab under sub heading Browser History select (Delete). Another menu pops up then select all the options that you want to clear and select delete.    

Book Flights Early

Airlines release flights in batches, usually winter and summer, register or sign up to their newsletter to be one of the first to know when flights are released. The earlier you book, the cheaper they will be!  Also be aware that there is a ‘golden window’ around 6 weeks to 3 months before the flight that airlines may reduce tickets based upon level of demand, this can also be a good time to book. Last minute flights are never cheap, business travellers’ book last minute; airlines know this so they hike the prices up.    

Consider a Package Holiday

Check out this holiday below with www.icelolly.com  it includes B&B for 7 nights in a 3 star in Torremolinos (10 minutes from Malaga city) PLUS return flights from Manchester for just 135 Euros pp, bargain!!     For flights only on the same dates with Easyjet, it is almost as much at 117 Euros return.  I know which one I would book!  

Student Discounts

There are loads of discounted travel tickets and holiday packages available to you if you are a student check out www.statravel.co.uk for cheap student fares. Check their website for savings on flights to Malaga but for real savings STA also offer great multi-stop packages, popular with students who don’t want the hassle of planning a round the world trip themselves.  Check out this example of just 2 of the multi trip options STA offer, you can see the price for students and under 26’s is cheaper than for adults.  STA can also sort out student discount cards and working visas as well as loads more useful stuff.

None English airlines

When we think about booking flights to Malaga we usually think of the usual airlines everyone uses...think outside of the box and go on the official website of the airport to check which airlines fly to Malaga.  I’ve done it for you for flights from Gatwick to Malaga, you can see ‘Norwegian Air’ is listed, many people still don’t know this airline flies to Malaga.  Not only are they an excellent airline with not such a ‘budget’ feel, they can also be cheaper too.

Be Flexible

Sometimes taking a flight with 1 stop can work out cheaper, of course it will add to your travelling time but check out Spanish airlines, ‘Iberia’ (www.iberia.com) and ‘Vueling’ (www.vueling.com) for potentially cheaper flights with a short stop in Barcelona. Beware of length of stop-over if choosing this option as you wouldn’t want to spend half of your day waiting around another airport. Take some of these tips onboard the next time your searching for that cheap flight and see if they can save you any pennies be sure to let me know any of your tips that have bagged you that discounted flight - happy flying!   Follow these guidelines on the infographic below to make sure you get the best price possible!

item.title: Weather Forecast
item.dc:creator: lionelk
item.content:encoded: Málaga is a city and a municipality, capital of the Province of Málaga, in the Autonomous Community of Andalucia, Spain. With a population of 567,433 in 2012, it is the second most populous city of Andalucia and the sixth largest in Spain. Málaga enjoys a subtropical–mediterranean climate. It has one of the warmest winters in Europe, with average temperatures of 17 °C (62.6 °F) during the day and 7–8 °C (45–46 °F) at night in the period from December through February. The summer season lasts about eight months, from April through November, although in the remaining four months temperatures sometimes reach around 20 °C (68.0 °F).
