wp:comment.wp:comment_content: Returned from a seven night stay at the Riu Costa Del Sol on 26th November 2017, your review us pretty much as accurate as is possible.....fantastic Hotel, Staff there could literally not do enough for the Guests....10/10

Returned from a seven night stay at the Riu Costa Del Sol on 26th November 2017, your review is pretty much as accurate as is possible.....fantastic Hotel, Staff there could literally not do enough for the Guests....10/10

Hey, so glad you took the time to comment on my review post having stayed there. It's invaluable to me to hear what other people think of something I've reviewed, whether they agree or not. It helps me to see what others look for in a holiday/hotel also.
I'm also really pleased you had a great experience and enjoyed your stay at the Riu, its a great hotel. Could you tell me, did you read my review before or after you stayed here? Did it sway your opinion on booking if you read it before you booked? Just interested to know...
Thanks Anna

hi Stuart. Thanks for reading the post and taking the time to comment. You must have stayed here just after us and I have to say I agree with what you said about this hotel. The cocktails did let it down a little as I mention in my review and yes we have also stayed in other Riu hotels and the entertainment was very samey. But this wouldn't stop me from staying here again as overall it was a fantastic well run, family resort.
Excellent saving you made on your 2018 booking too, great tip about signing up for the Riu member card!!! Enjoy your holiday, I hope it comes round quickly.

We stayed here in June 2017 and really enjoyed the hotel. At that stage, it was clear that the staff were adjusting to its new size and the volume of customers, but it really was a great experience with only a few niggles: The in-house entertainment is the same I've seen in EVERY Riu hotel I've been to since 2009! It never changes.... The cocktails weren't up to the usual standard- far too watery for some reason.
And we've booked up for next year, but this time directly with Riu as it was a much better price and the hotel is SO close to the airport, services with budget carriers.
One tip- always sign up for the Riu member card, even if you've booked through a travel agent. It's free ans the rewards points discount any direct booking you make with Riu. Saved us £400 on our booking!

Hi, thanks for reading my post. Some hotels actually close in November until the spring so it's worth checking with them. If the Riu is open, it's in a great spot, opposite the beach and close to bars and restaurants and will most definitely have very few kids there, maybe some pre-school aged kids but nothing to speak of. The area is popular with golfers and a more mature crowd off season.

Hi thank you so much for your review is helped me so much in choosing this hotel and I am so looking forward to our holiday stay in there on the March 7th all the reviews that you have wrote is everything that I was interested in and I look forward to reading anymore about your holidays

Hello we are wondering if you could help, We normally travel to the area in November and usual stay in the Torremolinos area in an adult only hotel on a half board basis, we've enjoyed that style of holiday, however by way of a change and looking to be abit more money conscious this year, and having just read your great review, was wondering how busy with children it would be in November / early December, whilst I appreciate its school term time, is it likely to be much quieter? (we are grandparents) but notice it seems to highly geared to families, we look to have a week away from the youngers once a year and this seem to fit the bill do you have any knowledge on this ?

Hi Anna, me and my fiancee are looking to go to the Costa del sol on the 28th of September for 2 weeks we've never been there before but we are hoping to visit alot of the different areas when we're there to hopefully choose a area to relocate too in a couple of years. We don't like staying in high rise hotels(probably something to do with my fear of heights) any suggestions of what area to base ourselves to go and visit the different areas when we're there please we're both 45 years old don't want it to busy or noisy but walking distance to the quiter bars,restaurants etc.. because we wont have a vehicle? Thanks Chris.

Hi Joanne, thanks for reading my post and your comment. As long as the hotel has guests they will provide entertainment, sometimes during the day around the pool and also evenings too. In my experience there was a mini disco for the little ones some evenings, although your 1 year old may be a little young to fully appreciate it.
Regarding the drinks, because we were there such a short period of time, we only experienced the 'all inclusive' wine and beer. In the buffet restaurants it was on tap but at the bars they serve you fron bottles from memory, it may well have been the same wine as in the barrels though to be honest. There may be other/better drinks you can pay for as an extra if you get bored of the included options. Failing that, you are never far away from good bars and beach front restaurants which offer nice choices of Spanich wine for as little as €3 a glass. Enjoy your holiday!

Hi Anna,
Myself, my partner and my 1 year old are heading to this hotel for a week from Ireland at the end of November. Would you know if entertainment in the hotel is all year round or just during the spring/summer months?
Also, most importantly is it just the ‘on tap’ self-serve wine and beer that is included in the all inclusive or are the drinks you order from the bar also included?
Thank you for your thorough review 😊

Hi Chris, thanks for your message. I assume you are flying into Malaga airport? If so there are lot's of choices all along the coast. As you are here for two weeks, it might be an idea to split your time in more than one place, that way you will get to see more of the coast and getting around by bus and train is quite easy. Did you read my post on top 5 resorts? That might help you decide. One resort not mentioned in that post that i think you and your partner will love is La Cala de Mijas. It's 10 minutes in a taxi or you can take a bus from Fuengirola and is a great spot if you don't have a car. The resort is like a village, there's loads of bars, restaurants offering all types of cuisine, several supermarkets and a gorgeous beach with a lovely long 5km boardwalk which hugs the coastline, along it are many other bars, cafes and restaurants to stop off at day or night. La Cala isn't too busy end of September but busy enough to still have a lovely buzz about it and end of September is a perfect time of year to come. From La Cala you can take a bus into Fuengirola centre in one direction and in the opposite direction the bus goes all the way to MArbella, but you can hop off at any of the other resorts along the way. Ive put together a hotel search for you in La Cala, from the list, The Orange house is great, bang centre with a nice rooftop bar but be aware it has no pool but it's a stones throw from the beach. Also consider staying in Malaga for at least a few days, it's a fantastic city and you can reach it by train directly from the airport in under 10 minutes. It's not a huge city so again you can walk it easily, it has a nice beach and a beautiful marina too. Hope this helps, enjoy your stay.

item.title: Caminito del Rey Walk – 2025 Update on What you need to Know
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
The Caminito del Rey, which translates to ‘The Kings little Path’ was constructed in 1905 and was aptly named after King Alfonso XIII crossed the walk in 1921. The walkway fell into dis-repair and despite being closed to the public, people still found a way to cross it, resulting in many tragic deaths.  Until it’s restoration in 2015, the Caminito was often referred to as ‘The World’s most Dangerous Footpath’ and the ‘One of The World’s Scariest Hikes’. The Caminito re-opened in 2015 following a 4 year restoration project and is now much more of a scenic walk than the terrifying trek of years gone by. Since it re-opened around 300.000 tickets are sold annually for this famous walk, it even attracts celebrities. Recently UK celebrity chefs Gordon Ramsey, Gino D’acampo and Fred Sirieix filmed part of the popular ITV show ‘Gordon, Gino and Fred: Viva Espana! taking on the walk.  The trio were filmed crossing the notorious suspension footbridge, the ‘Puente del Rey’ with a terrified Gino hilariously crawling along while Gordon and Fred look on in hysterics. The walk is around 60km inland from the beautiful city of Malaga. It's over 7km long and is made up of forest paths and footbridges, most of which cling precariously to the gorge walls 100 metres above the River Guadalhorce. Still not convinced it’s safe enough?? If my ‘terrified of heights’ husband can do this trek, believe me, anyone can. :-)

Getting to the Caminito del Rey

Getting to the Caminito del Rey is easy, there are a number of different options to consider. Car - A pleasant drive through the Malaga countryside to El Chorro, depending on your start point, it should take less than 1.5 hours. Train - From Malaga's Maria Zambrano train station, direct to El Chorro. The journey takes around 50 minutes direct and trains run several times a day for between €3 and €5. Bus + ticket - By far the most stress free way to get to the Camino is to book a guided bus transfer with your entrance ticket to the walk included, this way someone else can take the hassle out of the planning. All you have to do is turn up at the meeting point at the agreed pick-up time.

Railway line running through the gorge

Tourists and locals have been coming to the area around the Caminito for years, especially in summer time when the turquoise reservoirs offer much needed respite from the hot sun. There are some great water sports including a giant inflatable water park on the lake from June to September. There are plenty quaint little campsites, b&b's and guest houses in the area known as the Guadalhorce valley.  The landscape is unique, breathtaking in fact and its all just so peaceful and calm.

How to book your tickets

Spaces are limited for the Caminito del Rey for safety reasons and they only allow around 50 people every half hour. Slots are released in 3 or 4 month batches and weekends get booked up quickly so there's no point in just turning up hoping to get a slot.  You really must book ahead. Booking is easy, just go to the calendar choose your date and time and select the number of tickets you want.  Pay with a credit card and print off the confirmation e-mail to take with you.

The journey begins - Camino del Rey

We finally did the walk on chilly but beautifully sunny Saturday afternoon in December, after our previous booking a year earlier was aborted when my daughter woke up covered in chicken pox spots that morning. Important! if you can’t make it for any reason, they don’t offer refunds or alternative dates.  It’s tough luck basically as we found out after we were a ‘no show’ the first time. Weather in Ardales, as it's in land can be a few degrees cooler in winter than down on the coast and in summer expect it to be hotter, so be sure to check the forecast.  On the day of our walk temperatures in Malaga were 16 degrees but only 12 degrees in Ardales that day. I was glad I threw an extra layer into the boot of the car just before we set off because with the blustery wind it felt much colder.

Arriving at the Caminito del Rey

The Camino del Rey walk is linea, you can only start the walk at one end, this is the North access point, you have to finish the walk at the South exit point.  For me the most logical thing to do if you arrive by car is this...follow road signs to the North entrance, park your car and start the walk through the entrance tunnel. When you finish the walk at the South end, directly opposite the Garganta Hotel is a bus stop. Buses run several times per hour and are none stop between the North and South points, taking around 15 minutes each way.  You can pay the driver in cash, the cost is €2.50 pp (correct price for 2023)  and the bus will take you right back to  the North access right where you started. The bus driver will only accept cash, no cards and it's worth bearing in mind that it runs between the hours of 7.40am and 7pm, it stops at El Kiosko restaurant at the North entrance. If you have time, I can personally recommend a well deserved pit-stop in the outdoor terrace bar of La Garganta Hotel, where you can rest your tired legs and marvel over the amazing walk you just completed.

North entrance (El Kiosko restaurant) and start of the walk

We wanted to grab a light bite before starting the walk which was scheduled for 2pm, and knew there were some restaurants at the North entrance. Restaurant El Kiosko overlooking the lake was the perfect choice as next to it is the tunnel which you need to go through to start the Caminito del Rey.  Here you can pick up take away drinks and snacks too but bear in mind after this point, there is nowhere else to buy refreshemnts.

Restaurant El Kiosko & place to pick up snacks at the North entrance.

We arrived about 12.30pm and ventured upstairs at El Kiosko where they had a huge open fire so we grabbed a table right next to it and ordered. Portions were huge and we found it a bit much before embarking on a 7k hike. There is a snack bar downstairs and also a grab and go type counter where you can pick up supplies like water, canned drinks, snack bars etc to take with you. There are also toilets downstairs at the entrance to the tunnel.

Roaring fire in restaurant El Kiosko

Allow yourself plenty of time

From this point (the tunnel), you still need to allow yourself 30 minutes before your time slot as this is NOT the start of the Caminito del Rey. This a 2.5 km scenic walk through forest to reach the starting point which will take 30 minutes at least. Once at the starting point there were already loads of people waiting and there are staff to check your tickets, give you helmets and put you in the correct group. There are a lot of people that are part of guided tours which you can also book through the website, the tours are in English and Spanish. Next they separated people into English and Spanish speakers for a brief safety instruction where the guide told us to allow around 2.5 hours to complete the walk, then you are off on your way.

One of the lakes near the Caminito

Almost immediately we came to a stretch of the route where the footpath changes to wooden slats secured on top of steel rods which are pinned into the side of the mountain. There’a a mesh fence and handrail about waist high and most of this is suspended around 100 feet up. It was only at this point I realised my husband of 12 years or so was actually really terrified of heights, this was real proper fear written all over his face. Obviously, I laughed and told him it was 100% safe and to get on with it as we had another 5km to go, we had already come too far to turn back. The scenery along the route is amazing, my husband missed out on most of it because he could barely look up or down. The vultures, buzzards and eagles circling above are ever present and I wondered if they were there waiting patiently for victims to fall. As mentioned, the footpath fell into disrepair years ago and was closed in 2000 as it was so dangerous.  You can actually see the original path complete with holes, rusty metal poles and huge sections missing right below as you walk the new pathway. Terrifying to think adrenaline junkies attempted this walk while it was in disrepair despite the €6000 fine not to mention the huge risk involved.  Memorials are displayed to acknowledge 4 of the climbers that lost their life....

Old and new path

No fear now though, It is completely safe once again and very well organised from start to finish.

The Walkway of Death

About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high, it is known as 'The Walkway of Death'. I've included a video showing a great overview of what to expect! https://youtu.be/9HJhwenwOf0 There are guides either side of the bridge making sure that everyone crosses safely, they will also give the option to turn back for those too scared.  From this point, you only have around 2km to go so turning back is not an option for most. I loved this part, it was such a great opportunity to take photos and video from all angles. Suspended mid air between the rock face with absolutely nothing interrupting your view.

Walk of nerves!

The Walkway of Death. Once safely on the other side and during the final km stretch, the Caminito takes a dramatic path along a very straight and narrow cliff, then finally comes back to solid ground for the final few hundred metres. There are some information boards explaining how and when it was built and about the restoration, stop and look at them as they really help you appreciate the almost impossible task of it's construction.

Map showing the route.

Getting back to your car

All that is left to do now is keep walking another few hundred metres until you arrive at El Chorro train station. Pass the car park and a camp site, then you'll see the train station on the left with a handy little bar to grab a quick drink. Next to the station is where you pick up the bus to take you right back to the start/North. There were already people waiting when we arrived and a bus had just pulled in however there was no room for us so we had to wait 30 minutes for the next one.

El Chorro Train station

If you have a little bit of time a fantastic place to grab a bite to eat and a drink is La Garganta Hotel and restaurant right opposite the bus stop. Walk round to the outside terrace for direct views of the Caminito and a well earned drink. I really wish I had known about this hotel before our visit as it's the perfect location to the Caminito del Rey to stay over for a night or two and explore the area more.  It has so much rustic charm and gorgeous views over the lake and the final stretch of the Caminito del Rey. The bus was punctual and the ride back to the car and North entrance took only about 15 minutes.  The bus takes you just past the car park and drops you right at El Kiosko and the entrance tunnel to the start of the route. All in all the walk took a total us of 2 hours 30 minutes, including the short walk leading to the start of the Caminito del Rey. If I could summarise, this walk is as close you will ever come to feeling like you are part of a Indiana Jones movie.  The clear glass viewing platform, if you dare to step onto it is a reminder of how unnaturally high up you are, even more apparent if you are afraid of heights. It is unlike any other place you will ever go to and even though some say it has lost its edge, if you are an adrenaline junkie then I believe you cannot come to the Malaga region and not walk the Caminito del Rey.

Essential Information

Bring plenty water, snacks and sunscreen Small backpack (large bags are not allowed) Comfortable clothing and footwear (hiking shoes are best but trainers are adequate) Pets are not allowed There are no toilets along the path The walk will occasionally close in the event of bad weather - refunds are not offered

The journey takes around 40 minutes direct and trains run several times a day for between €3 and €5.</p><p><a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/caminito-del-rey-l89646/caminito-del-rey-vip-guided-tour-with-transport-t207921/?partner_id=3056VBG&utm_medium=online_publisher">Bus + ticket</a> - By far the most stress free way to get to the Camino is to book a guided bus transfer with your entrance ticket to the walk included. This way someone else can take the hassle out of the planning, all you have to do is turn up at the meeting point at the agreed time to be picked up and taken there.</p><p> </p>[caption id="attachment_4391" align="aligncenter" width="597"]<img class="wp-image-4391 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/railway.jpg" alt="Railway through mountain" width="597" height="338" /> Railway line running through the gorge[/caption]<p>Tourists and locals have been coming to the <a href="https://malagatravelguide.net/hotels/costa-glamping/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">area around the Caminito</a> for years, especially in summer time when the turquoise reservoirs offer much needed respite from the hot sun. There are also water sports including a giant inflatable water park on the lake from June to September.</p><p>There are plenty quaint little <a href="https://booki.ng/2LBagvz" target="_blank" rel="noopener">campsites, b&b's and guest houses</a> in the area known as the Guadalhorce valley.  The landscape is unique, breathtaking in fact and its all just so peaceful and calm.</p><p>Recommended Hotels</p><h3>How to book your tickets</h3><p>Spaces are limited for the Caminito del Rey for safety reasons and they only allow around 50 people every half hour. Slots are released in 3 or 4 month batches and weekends get booked up quickly so there's no point in just turning up hoping to get a slot.  You really must book ahead.</p><p>Booking is easy, just go to the calendar <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/caminito-del-rey-l89646/caminito-del-rey-vip-guided-tour-with-transport-t207921/?partner_id=3056VBG&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank" rel="noopener">choose your date and time</a> and select the number of tickets you want.  Pay with a credit card and print off the confirmation e-mail to take with you.</p>[caption id="attachment_4392" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4392 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/sign-to-camino.jpg" alt="Start sign Caminito" width="593" height="335" /> The journey begins - Camino del Rey[/caption]<p>We finally did the walk on chilly but beautifully sunny Saturday afternoon in December, after our previous booking a year earlier was aborted when my daughter woke up covered in chicken pox spots that morning.</p><p>By the way, if you can’t make it for any reason, they don’t offer refunds or alternative dates.  It’s tough luck basically as we found out after we were a ‘no show’ the first time.</p><p>Weather in Ardales, as it's in land can be a few degrees cooler in winter than down on the coast and in summer expect it to be hotter, so be sure to check the forecast.  On the day of our walk temperatures in Malaga were 16 degrees but only 12 degrees in Ardales that day.</p><p>I was glad I threw an extra layer into the boot of the car just before we set off because with the blustery wind it felt much colder.</p><h3>Arriving at the Caminito del Rey</h3><p>The Camino del Rey walk is linea, you can only start the walk at one end, this is the North access point, you finish the walk at the South exit point.  For me the most logical thing to do if you arrive by car is this...drive to the <strong>North entrance</strong>, park your car and start the walk through the entrance tunnel.</p><p>When you finish the walk at the South end, directly opposite the Garganta Hotel is a bus stop, buses run several times per hour and run none stop between the North and South points, taking around 15 minutes each way.  You can pay the driver in cash, the cost is €2 pp (correct price for 2023)  and the bus will take you right back to  the North access right where you started.</p><p>If you have time however, I can personally recommend a well deserved pit-stop in the outdoor terrace bar of La Garganta Hotel, where you can rest your tired legs and marvel over the amazing walk you just completed.</p>[caption id="attachment_4393" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4393 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/tunnel.jpg" alt="North entrance and start of the walk" width="593" height="335" /> North entrance and start of the walk[/caption]<p>We wanted to grab a light bite before starting the walk which was scheduled for 2pm, and knew there were some restaurants at the North entrance. Restaurant El Kiosko overlooking the lake was the perfect choice as next to it is the tunnel which you need to go through to start the Caminito del Rey.  Here you can pick up take away drinks and snacks too, bear in mind after this point, there is nowhere else to buy refreshemnts.</p>[caption id="attachment_4394" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4394 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/el-kiosko.jpg" alt="Restaurant El Kiosko" width="593" height="335" /> Restaurant El Kiosko & place to pick up snacks at the North entrance.[/caption]<p>We arrived about 12.30pm and ventured upstairs at El Kiosko where they had a huge open fire so we grabbed a table right next to it and ordered. Portions were huge and we found it a bit much before embarking on a 7k hike.</p><p>There is a snack bar downstairs and also a grab and go type counter where you can pick up supplies like water, canned drinks, snack bars etc to take with you. There are also toilets downstairs at the entrance to the tunnel.</p>[caption id="attachment_4396" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4396 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/fire.jpg" alt="Restaurant El Kiosko open log fire" width="593" height="335" /> Roaring fire in restaurant El Kiosko[/caption]<h3>Allow yourself plenty of time</h3><p>From this point (the tunnel), you still need to allow yourself 30 minutes before your time slot as this is NOT the start of the Caminito del Rey. It’s a 2.5 km scenic walk through forest to reach the starting point which will take 30 minutes at least.</p><p>Once at the starting point there were already loads of people waiting and there are staff to check your tickets, give you helmets and put you in the correct group. There are a lot of people that are part of guided tours which you can also book through the website, the tours are in English and Spanish.</p><p>Next they separate people into English and Spanish speakers for a brief safety instruction where the guide told us to allow around 2.5 hours to complete the walk, then you are off on your way.</p>[caption id="attachment_4437" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4437 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/lake-at-car-park.jpg" alt="lake el Chorro" width="593" height="335" /> One of the lakes near the Caminito[/caption]<p>Almost immediately we came to a stretch of the route where the footpath changes to wooden slats secured on top of steel rods which are pinned into the side of the mountain. There’a a mesh fence and handrail about waist high and most of this is suspended around 100 feet up.</p><p>It was only at this point I realised my husband of 12 years or so was actually really terrified of heights, this was real proper fear written all over his face.</p><p>Obviously, I laughed and told him it was 100% safe and to get on with it as we had another 5km to go, we had come too far to turn back.</p><p>The scenery along the route is amazing, my husband missed out on most of it because he could barely look up or down. The vultures, buzzards and eagles circling above are ever present and I wondered if they were there waiting patiently for victims to fall.</p><p>As mentioned, the footpath fell into disrepair years ago and was closed in 2000 as it was so dangerous.  You can actually see the original path complete with holes, rusty metal poles and huge sections missing right below as you walk the new pathway.</p><p>Terrifying to think adrenaline junkies attempted this walk while it was in disrepair despite the €6000 fine not to mention the huge risk involved.  Memorials are displayed to acknowledge 4 of the climbers that lost their life....</p>[caption id="attachment_4397" align="aligncenter" width="589"]<img class="wp-image-4397 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/CAMINITO-DEL-REY-old-and-new-path.jpg" alt="old dangerous path Caminito" width="589" height="393" /> Old and new path[/caption]<p>No fear now though, It is completely safe once again and very well organised from start to finish.</p><h3>The Walkway of Death</h3><p>About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high known as 'The Walkway of Death'.</p><p>I've included a video showing a great overview of what to expect!</p><p>https://youtu.be/9HJhwenwOf0</p><p>There are guides either side of the bridge making sure that everyone crosses safely. These guides also give the option for those too scared the option to turn back</p><p>I loved this part, it was such a great opportunity to take photos and video from all angles. Suspended mid air between the rock face with absolutely nothing interrupting your view.</p>[caption id="attachment_4399" align="alignnone" width="592"]<img class="wp-image-4399 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/bridge-1.jpg" alt="Camino del Rey walk of death" width="592" height="326" /> Walk of nerves![/caption]<p>The Walkway of Death.</p><p>Once safely on the other side and during the final km stretch, the Caminito takes a dramatic path along a very straight and narrow cliff, then finally comes back to solid ground for the final few hundred metres.</p><p>There are some information boards explaining how and when it was built and about the restoration, stop and look at them as they helps you appreciate the almost impossible task of its construction.</p>[caption id="attachment_4400" align="aligncenter" width="593"]<img class="wp-image-4400 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/map.jpg" alt="Map el Chorro region" width="593" height="335" /> Map showing the route.[/caption]<h3>Getting back to your car</h3><p>All that is left to do is follow the signs for the El Chorro train station, its easy as its a straight road. Pass the car park and a camp site, then you'll see the train station on the left with a handy little bar to grab a quick drink.</p><p>Next to the station is where you pick up the bus to take you back to the start. There were already people waiting when we arrived and a bus had just pulled in however there was no room for us so we had to wait 30 minutes for the next one.</p>[caption id="attachment_4401" align="aligncenter" width="544"]<img class="wp-image-4401 size-full" src="https://malagatravelguide.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/El-Chorro-train-station.jpg" alt="El Chorro Train station" width="544" height="294" /> El Chorro Train station[/caption]<p>If you have a little bit of time a fantastic place to grab a bite to eat and a drink is <a href="https://booki.ng/2suWDFJ" target="_blank" rel="noopener">La Garganta Hotel</a> and restaurant right opposite the bus stop. Walk round to the outside terrace for direct views of the Caminito and a well earned drink.</p><p>I really wish I had known about this hotel before our visit as it's the perfect location to the Caminito del Rey to stay over for a night or two and explore the area more.  It has so much rustic charm and gorgeous views over the lake and the final stretch of the Caminito del Rey.</p><p>I've rounded up the <a href="https://bit.ly/CamDelRey" target="_blank" rel="noopener">best hotels and accommodation</a> ideally located to explore this amazing national park area</p><p>The bus was punctual and journey back to the car and north entrance took only about 15 minutes.  The bus takes you just past the car park and drops you right at El Kiosko and the entrance tunnel to the start of the route.</p><p>All in all the walk took a total us of 2 hours 30 minutes, including the short walk leading to the start of the Caminito del Rey.</p><p>If I could summarise, this walk is as close you will ever come to feeling like you are part of a Indiana Jones movie.  The clear glass viewing platform, if you dare to step onto it is a reminder of how unnaturally high up you are, even more apparent if you are afraid of heights.</p><p>It is unlike any other place you will ever go to and eve though some say it has lost its edge, if you are an adrenaline junkie then I believe you cannot come to the Malaga region and not walk the Caminito del Rey.</p><h3>Essential Information</h3><p>Bring plenty water, snacks and sunscreen</p><p>Small backpack (large bags are not allowed)</p><p>Comfortable clothing and footwear (hiking shoes are best)</p><p>Pets are not allowed</p><p>There are no toilets along the path</p><p>The walk will occasionally close in the event of bad weather - refunds are not offered</p>__TVE_SHORTCODE_RAW___

Hi, No not all of it is boardwalk, as i mentioned in the post, the start of the walk is though forest type terrain so there are some ups and downs and some uneven paths. The boardwalk part has a rail but also the suspension bridge which crosses from one part of the cliff to the other does move around quite a bit especially if it is windy. It might be worth you doing it first then booking it with your dad if you think he will manage. I really wouldn't like to say to be honest but you definitly need good mobility and balance to do it. From memory there aren't many stairs and steps though.
Thank you for your kind words, it means a lot. I do hope you get to do the walk, please let me know what you think of it.

Hi Paul, that's amazing, thanks so much for the feedback, it's so nice to hear that I have helped someone have a great experience. Im glad you enjoyed the Camino, it's hard to put into words how breathtaking it is don't you think? Honestly, thanks for taking the time to let me know.

Hi Mandy, No you definitely don't need to do it with a guide, it generally takes longer with the guide than if you were to do it on your own. There are some picnic benches along the way, but honestly not that many places to stop and take a break since much of the walk is too narrow to accomodate benches. Keep in mind that in August it is going to be very hot and you will need at least 3 hours to complete it.

Hi we hoped to do this hike in May but when attempting to book i see there is an age restriction!I am 66 and my husband is 72 and active and so are many over 65's but yet it states up to 65 only! Is this a strict rule?

This is from the official website: Crutches and/or canes (including hikers) are not allowed. The minimum age for access is 8 years old, and must be accredited with an official document at the entrance to the site.. Would you mind showing me where you read about the age restriction so i can look into this further. Thank you.

Hi Anna Thank you for this - I am coming to do the walk at the end of March and wondering if the whole route is boardwalk or whether there are also areas that are loose rocks or gravel etc? And is it lots of up and down...up and down on the stairs or mainly flat/hilly?
My dad is partially sighted and will be fine if the path is always a walk with a rail, but would struggle if there are loose rocks. His mobility is fine, going up and down stairs. How many stairs would you say there are?

item.title: Room Mate Valeria Malaga – Unpretentious Luxury
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
Room Mate Valeria is arguably one of the most popular places to stay in Malaga. If a boutique style, urban hotel with a fab rooftop bar is your thing; then Valeria should be on your shortlist.

Location

The location of the Valeria is pretty unbeatable for a city centre hotel.  Boasting fantastic views over the port and Malaga's own version of The London eye just a stone's throw away.  

This upscale hotel is just about a 5 minute walk in any direction to all of Malaga's hot spots, as well as the train station making getting to the hotel easy if you are arriving by plane.  

The train takes just 12 minutes from the airport station to Malaga-Centro Alameda station and they operate every 30 minutes. No need to pre-book, just buy a ticket from one of the ticket machines when you arrive at the airport station, they have an English language option available too.

The attractive new Marina development, otherwise known as Muelle Uno attracts many cruise ships with passengers seeking southern Spain's year round warm climate.

There's a huge choice of places to eat, drink and shop around the Marina and it's really pretty after dark when twinkling lights light up over the bay.

The Marina, Malaga Cathedral and the Moorish Alcazaba Fortress are all just 300 metres from the the hotel.  The sandy beach of Malaga can be reached in around 20 minutes on foot.

The main shopping area off Malaga's most famous street, Calle Marques de Larios is just 200 metres away where you will find many high street and designer boutiques. Rest your legs from all that shopping and grab a table at one of the outdoor terrace cafes and watch the world go by over nice glass of traditional Malaga wine.

Style of Hotel

From the outside, the hotel building has been tastefully restored with a cool urban grey facade. It fits in nicely with the other typically 18th century 'Malaga' style buildings around it.

Inside the calming tropical blue and green theme of the lobby and reception area is instantly welcoming. It's design was inspired by the gardens just outside the hotel and the large green leaf print covers the walls and cushions adorning sofas and comfy lounge chairs throughout the hotel.

Rooms and Suites

Accommodation ranges from basic rooms, family rooms sleeping a maximum of 4 and also deluxe suites boasting a separate living room and a generous 42sqm of space.  Rooms are spread over 4 floors and some have balconies.

Room decor is quite bold with either blue or green striped wall paper, perhaps not to everyone's taste, but it works. The bed in our standard room was super comfy with lovely plush pillows and good quality bed linen.

All rooms have en suite bathrooms with a super high pressure shower and are equipped with good quality toiletries, in fact some of the nicest we've sampled in a hotel.

Bonus points to Room mate for the conditioner, very few hotels provide it so I was one very happy girl, ladies you know what I mean!

Eats and Drinks

One of the biggest draws of the Valeria is the attractive rooftop bar and pool area. Malaga is becoming quite synonymous for it's selection of rooftop terrace bars and who doesn't love a gin & tonic watching the sun setting!

While the Valeria's terrace is not huge it is well laid out, the pool is very small so not an ideal choice if you want to swim but perfect for a cooling dip.

Comfy lounge beds are a nice addition and there are also plenty of tables and chairs for sitting with a drink, some with high stools for taking in those amazing views.

The background music on the rooftop is nice and ambient and the Mojitos are to die for, expertly made and absolutely delicious. You could argue that drinks prices are perhaps slightly higher than other bars around but as the setting is so beautiful it's worth splurging a bit here.  Did I mention the Mojitos....

Breakfast Buffet

There's nothing I like more than a good hotel breakfast and the Valeria's offering did not let me down.  A great selection of juices, cereals, breads, pastries and cold cuts and of course eggs, bacon and good quality 'bangers' too.

All was extremely well cooked and more importantly, fresh! While the breakfast selection and quality was very good, I was slightly disappointed to find it was in a a basement room with no natural light.

Valeria have done a great job of making this room nice with clever use of lighting and attractive furnishings.

Extra Amenities

The Valeria has a small gym available for guests which is open 24 hours a day.

To appeal to business travelers the hotel has an events manager available to guests or visitors wishing to book one of the meeting rooms or to help organise and plan an event.

In addition there is Wifi throughout the hotel, a mini bar in each room, luggage storage and ticket sales at the front desk for some of the best attractions in the area.

There is no parking facility within the hotel, however there are many public car parks nearby.

Family Friendly

The Hotel has a few family rooms, sleeping a maximum of 4 people however most rooms are for a standard 2.  We did see a couple of kids during our stay, although I'd say this hotel is better suited to adults.

Families with younger children would perhaps be more suited to a resort style hotel with dedicated children's facilities.

Value for Money

Prices for a standard start from around €100 in low season with an additional charge for breakfast.  

The hotel is unpretentiously luxurious and service is flawless throughout.  Luxury bed linens and bathroom amenities, lovely rooftop bar for evening drinks and the location and proximity to everything are all what makes the Room-mate Valeria stand out among the crowd.

It's excellent for money when you factor all of that in, even in high season.

​

item.title: Only YOU Hotel Málaga: Our Favourite Urban Oasis in the Heart of the City
item.dc:creator: administrator
item.content:encoded:
Perfect location in the heart of Malaga: Only YOU

By: MálagaTravelGuide.net Team | Locals sharing real insights from the sunny south of Spain

As Málaga locals who live just a stone’s throw from the Alameda Principal, we’ve seen the city evolve dramatically over the last decade. From sleepy seaside town to a thriving cultural hotspot, Málaga has become a sought-after destination for savvy travelers—and Only YOU Hotel Málaga is a prime example of the new wave of hospitality redefining the city.

Having visited this hotel multiple times (sometimes for staycations, sometimes just to sip cocktails on the rooftop), we can say this place isn’t just another hotel—it’s an experience. So if you're wondering where to stay in Málaga that blends local flavour with boutique luxury, keep reading.

 Location, Location, Location: The Beating Heart of Málaga

One of the biggest selling points of Only YOU Hotel Málaga is its unbeatable location. Nestled on Calle Alameda Principal, the hotel sits at the edge of Málaga's Old Town, with views over the port and easy access to everything that matters.

From the front door, you’re just steps away from:

  • Calle Larios – Málaga’s main shopping street
  • Atarazanas Market – A sensory delight for foodies
  • Muelle Uno – The waterfront promenade lined with shops and restaurants
  • Picasso Museum & Alcazaba – Cultural highlights within a 10-minute walk
[tcb-script src="https://www.booking.com/affiliate/prelanding_sdk"][/tcb-script] [tcb-script](function () {var BookingAffiliateWidget = new Booking.AffiliateWidget({"iframeSettings": {"selector": "bookingAffiliateWidget_c7f9e17f-d9b6-4911-b6c1-44ac6d27a4ac","responsive": true},"widgetSettings": {"ss": "Málaga, Andalucía, Spain","latitude": 36.721138,"longitude": -4.422028,"zoom": 14,"customMarkerTitle": " Only YOU"}});})();[/tcb-script]

 Rooms with Personality: Art Deco Meets Andalusian Chic

We’ve toured several of the hotel’s 93 rooms, and each one has a unique character. Expect a tasteful blend of Mediterranean tones, Art Deco details, and smart layouts that make even the standard rooms feel luxe. From rain showers to plush robes and branded toiletries, every touch feels thoughtful.

Pro Tip: Ask for a room with a terrace overlooking the port. There’s nothing like watching the sun rise over the sea with an Americano in hand.

Room Features We Love:

  • Soundproof walls (great for the city center)

  • Dreamy bedding that makes getting up difficult

  • Locally sourced mini-bar treats

  • Rooms for couples, solo travelers, and even pets!

Rooftop Magic: Lolita Skyview Pool & Lounge

Let's plan your perfect holiday in the Costa del Sol

Hi I'm Suzy! Let me help you discover the beautiful Costa del Sol. I've compiled a FREE resource guide to list my top family resorts, things to do and places to visit. 

VIP Resource List

Let's Plan Your Perfect Costa Holiday

Wanna sip cocktails on a rooftop bar, soak up the rays on a golden beach or make your own chocolate bars in a quaint Spanish village? With over 11 years living in the Costa del Sol I've got you covered. Let's get started...

New? Start Here!

For a quick start download the free VIP resource list. I've compiled must see, do and stay in an easy to read A4 sheet you can print off. I've done the hard work so you don't have to.

Guides

Whats the best resort for you? Easy to read blog posts that will help you make the right decision on where to stay on the Costa del Sol. 

WHERE TO STAY

No one likes getting ripped off, and even if your not Donald Trump you can still snag a top apartment or hotel.  Its all about location baby!

Best Hotels on the Costa del Sol

Let's plan your perfect holiday in the Costa del Sol

Hi I'm Suzy! Let me help you discover the beautiful Costa del Sol. I've compiled a FREE resource guide to list my top family resorts, things to do and places to visit. 

VIP Resource List

Let's Plan Your Perfect Costa Holiday

Wanna sip cocktails on a rooftop bar, soak up the rays on a golden beach or make your own chocolate bars in a quaint Spanish village? With over 11 years living in the Costa del Sol I've got you covered. Let's get started...

New? Start Here!

For a quick start download the free VIP resource list. I've compiled must see, do and stay in an easy to read A4 sheet you can print off. I've done the hard work so you don't have to.

Guides

Whats the best resort for you? Easy to read blog posts that will help you make the right decision on where to stay on the Costa del Sol. 

WHERE TO STAY

No one likes getting ripped off, and even if your not Donald Trump you can still snag a top apartment or hotel.  Its all about location baby!

Let's plan your perfect holiday in the Costa del Sol

Hi I'm Suzy! Let me help you discover the beautiful Costa del Sol. I've compiled a quick resource list of the top family resorts, things to do and places to stay. 

Quick Start Resource List

Let's Plan Your Costa Holiday

Sip cocktails on a rooftop bar, soak up the rays on a golden beach or make your own chocolate bars in a quaint Spanish village? With over 11 years living in the Costa del Sol I've got you covered...

Discover the best Resorts on the Costa del Sol

Stay up to date with the latest reviews & top holiday tips and get more out of your holiday

Some Popular Posts

1

7 of The Most Authentic Flamenco shows in Andalucia

The word ‘Flamenco’ conjures up images of swarthy skinned dancers in colourful gypsy style dresses with silk shawls performing a type of mysterious dance.  Accompanied by male guitarists and singers in dark suits.

1

CAMINITO DEL WAY - 'walkway of death'

About 2km from the end as the path snakes around a bend it reaches a crucial point where walkers cross from one side of the gorge to the other.  The only way to do this is by walking over a suspended bridge about 10 metres in length and hundreds of metres high known as ‘The Walkway of Death'.

1

INSIDERS TIPS TO EXPLORE AND ENJOY MALAGA CITY

Malaga city is a fantastic blend of both modern and traditional, from the 11th century Alcazaba Fortress standing proud above the city; to the impressive new marina complete with its trendy bars, restaurants and shops.

Fab Places to Stay

What's your tipple ... 5 Star Luxury on a super yacht or glamping in your private yurt?
